## Paris 4-Day City Break for 2 Adults
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg

A relaxed Paris plan for **2026-09-12 to 2026-09-15** that keeps each day to **2 major attractions max**, favors **walking**, and includes **at least one low-cost meal option daily**. Budget is set to stay around **€1,200 total excluding flights** for 2 adults.

## Day-by-Day Paris Itinerary and Budget Fit
| Day | Focus | Major Stops | Low-Cost Meal Option | Est. Day Cost for 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sep 12 | Central Paris + classic art | Louvre Museum; Seine riverside walk | Baguette sandwich + pastry from a boulangerie | €220–€300 |
| Sep 13 | Left Bank + gardens | Musée d’Orsay; Luxembourg Gardens | Crêpes or falafel in the Latin Quarter | €180–€260 |
| Sep 14 | Montmartre + local neighborhoods | Sacré-Cœur; Montmartre stroll | Market picnic or kebab/plat du jour | €160–€240 |
| Sep 15 | Historic core + farewell | Île de la Cité; Sainte-Chapelle or Notre-Dame exterior | Sandwich lunch before departure | €140–€220 |

## Paris Itinerary by Day
### Day 1: Louvre and Seine Stroll
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, then head to the **Louvre** for one major museum visit; focus on a few wings instead of trying to see everything.
- Afternoon: Walk the **Tuileries** and along the **Seine** toward Pont Neuf and Île de la Cité.
- Food: Grab a **boulangerie lunch** — sandwich, quiche, and dessert — for a budget-friendly start.
- Budget note: Museum tickets + transport + casual dinner should keep this day comfortably moderate.

### Day 2: Musée d’Orsay and the Left Bank
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/brush.svg
- Morning: Visit **Musée d’Orsay** for Impressionist and 19th-century art.
- Afternoon: Walk through **Luxembourg Gardens** and browse the Latin Quarter streets.
- Food: Choose **crêpes**, a **falafel wrap**, or a simple student-menu lunch.
- Budget note: This is one of the best-value days because most of it is walkable and low-transport.

### Day 3: Montmartre and Local Paris
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- Morning: Explore **Sacré-Cœur** and the hilltop views.
- Afternoon: Wander **Montmartre** lanes, small squares, and artist streets at an easy pace.
- Food: Do a **market picnic** with cheese, fruit, bread, and drinks, or choose a cheap **plat du jour**.
- Budget note: Keep this day light and scenic; it’s ideal for enjoying neighborhoods rather than paid attractions.

### Day 4: Île de la Cité Farewell
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- Morning: Walk **Île de la Cité** and the riverbanks early for quieter streets.
- Afternoon: Visit **Sainte-Chapelle** if you want one final paid highlight, or keep it free with a Notre-Dame exterior stop and nearby stroll.
- Food: Have a **sandwich lunch** near your departure area to avoid a rushed sit-down meal.
- Budget note: Keep souvenirs light and use the final day for flexible timing.

## Budget Plan for 2 Adults
- Lodging: **€500–€700** for 3 nights in a practical mid-range hotel or apartment
- Food: **€240–€360** with one low-cost meal daily and a few nicer dinners
- Attractions: **€120–€220** depending on museum choices and whether you book timed entries
- Local transport: **€40–€80** using metro, walking, and occasional taxis
- Buffer: **€100–€150** for coffee, snacks, or small extras
